title.narrative: Bolivia: Improving Employability and Labor Income of Youth Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Improving Employability and Labor Income of Youth Project for Bolivia is to improve employability and labor income of poor youth by supporting the expansion of the skills development programs in selected cities. There are two components to the project, the first component being improving and expanding the skills development programs. This component includes three sub-components: improving and expanding the Mi Primer Empleo Digno Program (MPED) in selected cities; implementing the pilot Micro Entrepreneurs Skills Training and Technical Assistance Program (MESTTA) in selected cities; and implementing the pilot remedial secondary education program in selected cities. Finally, the second component is the strengthening the implementation arrangements to administer, monitor and evaluate skills development programs. This component includes two sub-components: strengthening the implementation arrangements and the institutional capacity of the MTEPS to administer and coordinate the skills development programs; and strengthening the institutional capacity of Economic and Social Policy Analysis Unit (UDAPE) to improve the evaluation of the skills development programs.
The objective of the Project is to improve employability and labor income of poor youth by supporting the expansion of the Skills Development Programs in Selected Cities.

title.narrative: Increase in the placement rate of PMEIL beneficiaries in a job with at least minimum salary one year after completing the on-the-job training.

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved. </p>

<p>The impact evaluation shows that the activity had a positive impact on the future placement rate. The young people who benefited from job insertion though the PMEIL had a higher chance of obtaining employment than the individuals in the control group. The impact evaluation showed that only 5.5 percent of participants were employed before joining the program and 65.7 percent of them was employed in February 2020. In comparison to the control group, the increase is approximately 20 percetage points in the employment rate, which represents an improvement of 47 percent compared to the value of the control group.</p>

<p>This indicator was revised during the restructuring to make a reference to the PMEIL's on-the-job training/job insertions. </p>
